name: Salt Lake City International Airport
before:
Four miles west of downtown Salt Lake City, this is Utah's main way in and out, and by a long margin the busiest airport in the state. It handled just over 28.3 million passengers in 2024, an all-time record, and runs around 343 scheduled nonstop departures a day to 93 cities across North America, South America, Asia and Europe.

Much of that traffic exists because Delta Air Lines uses it as a hub, so plenty of travellers pass through on connections rather than stopping in the city. The rest are heading for the Intermountain West and the ski country, national parks and canyon roads that surround it, or for business in a metro area where nearly 1.3 million jobs sit within a 30-minute drive.

It has a good reputation for reliability. The airport has consistently ranked high among major US airports for on-time departures and arrivals and for its low cancellation rate, which matters if you are connecting onward. It is a joint civil-military site, owned by the City of Salt Lake City and run by the municipal Department of Airports, with the smaller Provo and Ogden-Hinckley airports serving the same region.
after:
Five miles north west of downtown Salt Lake City, this is by far the busiest airport in Utah. It handled just over 28.1 million passengers in 2025, slightly down on the 2024 record. The airport says it has nonstop flights to about 100 destinations, including Delta's to Amsterdam, London and Paris.

Delta Air Lines uses it as a hub and carries more than half of the airport's passengers. For skiers, ten resorts are less than an hour's drive away.

It has a good reputation for reliability. In the year to July 2026 it ranked first among major US airports for on-time departures and arrivals and second for fewest cancellations, which matters if you are connecting onward. It is a joint civil-military site, owned by the City of Salt Lake City and run by the municipal Department of Airports, with the smaller Provo and Ogden-Hinckley airports serving the same region.

claims.claim: The New SLC completes on 27 October 2026 with 94 gates
claims.why: Held back: new, replaces nothing (the old text says nothing of the terminal). The operator said on 23 July 2026 that the final phase of The New SLC, seven more gates (for United plus two common-use gates), opens on 27 October 2026, for a total of 94 gates, at a total cost of $5.1 billion; its overview describes one terminal and two concourses, A and B. Wikipedia agrees (11 more gates in fall 2026, 94 in all). Worth adding if Andy wants the terminal described: the long concourses and the tunnels between them matter to connecting passengers.
